1. The Learned Advocates for the appellant/insurance company as well as the
respondents/claimants are present.

2. The instant appeal had been filed against the judgment dated 28th February, 2023 passed by the Learned Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Additional District and Sessions Judge, 1st Court at Asansol, District- Paschim Bardhaman in MAC Case No.22 of 2016 under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. An application under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act had been filed for the death of the victim in an accident which occurred on 27th May, 2009 at about 14.30 hours at Suri Road (NH60) near Tilpara Cannal.
The victim was a pillion rider on a motor cycle bearing registration No WB38S/0667 which was hit by the offending truck bearing registration No. WB/37-9991.
The victim sustained severe injuries and was shifted to Sadar Hospital Suri wherein he succumbed to the injuries.

4. The Learned Advocate representing the appellant/insurance company submitted The National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Saraswati Dhibar & Ors on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88290851/

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Saraswati Dhibar & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 the Learned Tribunal erroneously did not consider the delay of 30 days in filing the complaint and the charge-sheet was filed after three years of the institution of the case being Suri P.S. Case No. 143/09 dated 26.06.2009 under Section 297/338/427/304(A) of the Indian Penal Code.
The delay in filing the written complaint as well as the filing of the charge- sheet exonerated the appellant/insurance company from paying the compensation amount.

5. The Learned Advocate representing the respondents/claimants submitted in view of the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court as well as this Hon'ble Court, a delay of 30 days in filing the written complaint due to certain extraneous and probable circumstances will not affect or debar the victim from receiving the compensation amount under the statute.
6. The Learned Tribunal had granted a sum of Rs. 4,78,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6 per cent per annum from the date of filing of the claim application.

7. The Learned Advocate for the respondent/insurance company did not dispute the occurrence of the accident nor the other ancillary issues including the validity of the driving licence and insurance policy etc.
8.

Considering the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court in Urmila Halder v. The New India Assurance Company Ltd1. and the same being affirmed by the Supreme Court in Special Leave Petition2 and the notification dated 22nd May, 2018, the appellants/claimants are entitled to Rs.5,00,000/- of just compensation with regard to second schedule 1(a) and notification dated 22nd May, 2018 and also the aforesaid observations of the High Court at Calcutta and the Hon'ble Supreme Court

, the second schedule 1(a) is as follows: -

Compensation payable in case of Death shall be five lakh rupees."
2019(2)TAC 143 Special Leave Petition(Civil) No. 6260 of 2019 9.
The delay of 30 days to file the written complaint will not affect the rights of the claimants to receive the compensation amount.

The impugned judgment passed by the aforesaid tribunal is modified to the extent of Rs. 22,000/- (Rs.5,00,000-Rs.4,78,000/-) along with interest to be paid at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of filing of the application till the date of its actual realization.

The Learned Advocate for the appellants/claimants submitted to have received the compensation of Rs. 4,78,000/-.
10.

The Learned Advocate for the appellant/insurance company is to deposit the balance sum of Rs.
22,000/- along with 6 % per cent interest per annum from the date of filing of the claim application before the office of the Learned Registrar General, High Court Calcutta within four weeks from the date of passing of this order.
